utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session now. We still have the issue of the report of Professor Zecevic. As far as the Chamber understands, the confusion is about what is the report of Dr. Zecevic. Is that everything, that means curriculum vitae and witness statements and OTP Exhibits P3276, that is the report itself, and the supplemental information sheet of the 22nd of November and a similar one of the 1st of March. Because I do understand that the Defence takes the view that whatever would relate in the four documents not being the report itself, should be redacted as well, so as to take out any reference to subjects other than the one on which the question -- on which the witness was questioned. May I first ask Mr. Ierace or Mr. Stamp, is it just a report or are all the five documents I just mentioned part of what is tendered by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May it please you, -- I beg your pardon. Mr. President, Your Honours, it is all five documents which we submit to the Court as a full statement pursuant to Rule 94 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since I did understand that the remaining problem is in the redacting the other four documents, apart from the specific report of the witness itself, I would then invite the parties again to see whether they could agree on what parts of the other documents should be redacted as well. But before inviting you to do so, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Since Mr. Stamp knows this because I have written it, it is not just that. The first page in question has to be reviewed and corrected in a sense that we came before you for everything that interested other elements, that some of these shellings should be redacted, some of the bombardments should be redacted. Yes, we know that the attack on the Sarajevo TV building, which is mentioned on page 1. I don't know whether Mr. Stamp would like to say something. His microphone is on. Which is mentioned on the first page of the document is also -- precisely something which was referring to air attacks and we have decided that these are not the subject of this report. And we find it on the first page. I think that indicate -- I put that very clearly in the four lines where I said that the first page of the statement also has to be redacted, since it is referring to an element which has to be excluded. This is actually just one line. It has to be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, is it a problem of malcommunication or is there a problem of principle?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There might be a minor problem of principle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would be?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It appears that the complaint about the first page and we are not exactly sure the complaint is, but it appears to be a statement that during the war, I was -- "during the world war, I conducted only two investigations. One was the attack of the TV building on the 20th of June, 1995 and the other was the investigation of the shelling of the marketplace of the 5th of February, 1994." That is a reference to something else which my friend seeks to redact. To redact the brief statement that one of the investigations was an investigation in 1995, that is all that is said, would really take away from the context of the sentence and it really --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean that it doesn't give any information as apart from that an investigation was done, which might relate to the experience of the expert and gives no information as to what the investigation resulted in or -- well, whatever, it's just indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It is just a part of a sentence. If I may just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. I will ask Mr. Piletta-Zanin to respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: As I understand it, the issue of redactions arose because the Defence indicated quite rightly that the report of, in respect to the investigations of the 25th of January 1995, were not relevant to the issues before this Court. And that was raised in respect only to this part of the full report. In other words, only to the statement of the 27th of February 1996, which is one of the documents in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That, all of that reference, has been redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. If, as we hear it from Mr. Stamp, this doesn't bring anything to the case. I believe that this is an excellent reason to redact this. I am still talking about the first page. Now the other objection which is much more fundamental is if we are supposed to admit these documents as being reports of an expert or a quasi-expert, the least of the thing it would be to have these documents signed. Now you have seen it just like myself, that these documents for a large part have not been signed. The only document that we see signed are those that are witness statements, but the rest of the documents have not been signed. Therefore, this is a problem of principle. So this is a basic objection on the nature of what has been produced by the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the -- yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Briefly. The complaint about the all the pages of the documents being signed is irregular and I would submit, cannot be reasonable deemed by this Court because it is not timely. It could have been made, if it was important that every page be signed, a long time ago. The only thing it is respectfully submitted, Mr. President, Your Honours, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. which comes in for consideration is the Defence objection made that the references to the TV building investigation be redacted. It is now too late to make a complaint, it is respectfully submitted that every single page in an expert report or as it is described in the Rule, the full statement of the expert be signed. If that issue would have been ordered in a more timely way --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you. I don't think that we ever accepted on the principle these reports. I think we already said that. If we are to say to the Prosecution that it has not been signed and everybody can see that this has not been signed. This is asking too much of the Defence. We cannot accept these documents. They haven't been signed even if they come from an expert. An expert has to sign his expert report. Otherwise, it's just a piece of paper, unsigned piece of paper. And we believe that we cannot accept unsigned pieces of paper even if this comes from an expert. This seems to be an obvious question and I think the reason is obvious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The original of the expert report itself, I see signatures on every single page or is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which documents are you talking about, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am talking about the document P3276, as it appears in the original language. That is what starts with, "Elaborat." [phoen] I see the bottom of each page I see a --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please give us an ERN number, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems to be 02115533. It is the report itself, "The Study of the Circumstances and Causes of the Massacre at Markale Market."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. What was your question, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was that I see a signature on the bottom of each page of the exhibit I just mentioned. It is the report --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is true --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The signatures were missing and I am wondering what --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but all of the attachments that we have, for instance, four and five, have -- are not the documents. It is about these attachments that I am talking about. These are documents that on one hand are not linked to the report as such, in a material way or even physically if I dare say this, and on the other hand, they are very distinct from the report, the supplementary information sheet. So I don't think we can admit that as being a report from an expert. We have heard a quasi-expert and this is where our objection lie. The way it has been presented, this is not acceptable for us and I believe for your Chamber. That is why I said the other day, only over my dead body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No would have been enough. But so we are just talking about the signatures under the supplemental information sheets. The Chamber will consider the matter and --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise. We are also talking about the first page of the statements, since we are saying anything that is linked regarding the agreement with the Prosecution, with the attack that is mentioned in the document, the Sarajevo TV Building. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, while we are in open session, might I indicate that we have significant problems with the timetable in relation to next week. Steps are being taken at the moment to fill some gaps. I will update you later on today. In the meantime, two days ago I asked if the Defence could inform us if they could have their artillery expert here on the 10th of July and perhaps the 12th of July. I still have not heard. I would be grateful if they could simply let us know that that that would assist us in restructuring the timetable. Thank you

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I inform the parties before giving an opportunity to Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that we will not sit on the 12th. We will sit on the 10th of July, but we will not sit on Friday, the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence agree with the date of the 10th of July. If this is of course suitable for the colleagues, since you just mentioned that the 12th of July we would not be sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would be grateful if my learned colleague could inform us of the availability of the expert on the 9th as well, given the information which we have just received. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we will check about the 9th of July. The point is that the only thing that can be the problem can be making sure that he comes regarding his transport because of the summer period, when there are more problems to do with transport than usual, to do with airlines. But in any case, the 9th and the 10th, it seems that the Defence may accept this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Very grateful, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since Mr. Ierace wanted to raise some matters that are linked to the answers, could we please know when we are going to have the answers to the last questions that we asked of the Prosecution on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know what these questions are about. If there is any remaining problem after the break, I would like to hear about it. We will then turn again into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 7.05 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 28th day of June, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
